title: Installation
text: Several modules optional dependencies loaded demand (listed Suggests). Key ones: Bioconductor — GenomicRanges, IRanges, ChIPseeker, clusterProfiler, Rsubread, rtracklayer, etc. Install via BiocManager::install(). Batch correction — sva (ComBat), limma (removeBatchEffect). Annotation — org.Hs.eg.db, AnnotationDbi. CIBERSORT — Source code must obtained separately authors. See Reference page. Quantile normalization — preprocessCore. Bioconductor packages unexpectedly unavailable installation, run BiocManager::valid() identify fix version mismatches.

title: Create Circos Plot — AETHER_create_circos
text: Creates circos plot prepared data, signal tracks showing genomic coverage across chromosomes. Supports multiple samples/groups customizable colors track organization.

title: Create Circos Plot — AETHER_create_circos
code: AETHER_create_circos(   circos_data,   genome = "hg38",   output = NULL,   split_by = "omics",   color_by = "track",   invert_gradient = FALSE,   colors = NULL,   track_height = 0.12,   track_margin = 0.01,   line_width = 1,   ideogram_height = 0.04,   title = NULL,   width = 10,   height = 10,   res = 300,   highlights = NULL,   highlight_padding = 0.005,   annotation_regions = NULL,   annotation_colors = NULL,   show_chords = TRUE,   chord_alpha = 0.5,   annotation_sector_size = 2e+08,   start_degree = 90,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Create Circos Plot — AETHER_create_circos
text: circos_data List AETHER_prepare_circos_data() containing bins, signal matrix, sample_info, chr_sizes. genome Character. Genome assembly name cytoband data (default = "hg38"). output Character string. Output file path. Format inferred extension: ".png" PNG, ".pdf" PDF. NULL, plot displayed saved. split_by Character vector specifying split tracks. Options: "omics" - one track per omics type (always applied) "group" - additionally split group "batch" - additionally split batch Can combine: c("omics", "group") creates one track per omics+group. Default "omics" . color_by Character string specifying color granularity. Options: "track" (default) - one base color per track, gradients samples "group" - colors keyed group name (e.g., "WT", "KO") "omics_group" - colors keyed omics_group (e.g., "ATACseq_WT") Allows finer color control track splitting. example, split_by="omics" color_by="omics_group" puts WT KO track different colors. multiple samples share color key, gradients generated. invert_gradient Logical. Controls gradient direction relative signal: FALSE (default) - highest signal = darkest color (plotted top) TRUE - lowest signal = darkest color (plotted top) colors Named character vector colors. Names match color_by scheme: color_by="track": names like "ATACseq", "CHIPseq" color_by="group": names like "WT", "KO" color_by="omics_group": names like "ATACseq_WT", "ATACseq_KO" NULL, assigns colors automatically. track_height Numeric. Height signal track fraction total radius (default = 0.12). track_margin Numeric. Margin tracks (default = 0.01). line_width Numeric. Width signal lines (default = 1.0). ideogram_height Numeric. Height chromosome ideogram (default = 0.04). title Character string. Plot title displayed center (default = NULL). width Numeric. Output width inches (default = 10). height Numeric. Output height inches (default = 10). res Numeric. Resolution PNG output DPI (default = 300). highlights Named list highlight definitions. element list : regions: data.frame chr, start, end columns tracks: character - track name(s) highlight, "" signal tracks color: hex color string (include alpha transparency, e.g., "#FF000033") Example: list("peaks" = list(regions = peaks_df, tracks = "ATACseq", color = "#FF000033")) highlight_padding Numeric. Padding highlights fraction chromosome length (default = 0.005, .e., 0.5% side). Increase make small regions visible. annotation_regions Data frame annotated regions chord connections. Must contain columns: chr, start, end, annotation. annotation column contain category labels (e.g., "Promoter", "Intron", "Exon"). Compatible APOLLO_annotate_peaks() output. User can simplify annotation labels passing. annotation_colors Named character vector colors annotation categories. Names match values annotation_regions$annotation. NULL, default colors used. show_chords Logical. TRUE (default), draw chord connections regions annotation sector. FALSE, show annotation sector without chords. chord_alpha Numeric. Transparency chord fill (0-1, default = 0.5). annotation_sector_size Numeric. Size annotation pseudo-chromosome base pairs (default = 2e8). Adjust visual balance. start_degree Numeric. Starting angle degrees first sector (default = 90, top/12 o'clock). Use smaller values rotate clockwise. annotation sector center-right (3 o'clock), try values around -50 -70 depending number chromosomes. verbose Logical. Print progress messages (default = TRUE).

title: Create Circos Plot — AETHER_create_circos
text: Invisibly returns NULL. Side effect creating plot.

title: Create Circos Plot — AETHER_create_circos
text: function creates circos plot : Outer ring: Chromosome ideogram labels alternating colors Inner rings: Signal tracks, independently scaled Track organization examples: split_by = "omics": ATACseq track, CHIPseq track split_by = c("omics", "group"): ATACseq_WT, ATACseq_KO, CHIPseq_WT, CHIPseq_KO split_by = c("omics", "batch"): ATACseq_b1, ATACseq_b2, etc. track independently scaled (y-axis) prevent squishing combining different omics types different signal ranges. Color assignment depends color_by parameter: color_by="track": One base color per track, gradient shades multiple samples (darkest = highest signal, plotted top) color_by="group": Colors assigned group name, allowing different colors within track color_by="omics_group": Colors assigned omics+group combination, e.g., "ATACseq_WT" "ATACseq_KO" can different colors even track split_by="omics" Samples always plotted order mean signal (lowest first, highest last top) preserve data visibility.

title: Create Circos Plot — AETHER_create_circos
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Prepare data circos_data <- AETHER_prepare_circos_data(   sample_sheet, chr_sizes, omics = c("ATACseq", "CHIPseq") )  # One track per omics (default) AETHER_create_circos(circos_data, output = "circos.png")  # Split by omics and group AETHER_create_circos(circos_data, output = "circos.png",                       split_by = c("omics", "group"))  # With centered title AETHER_create_circos(circos_data, output = "circos.png",                       title = "Multi-omics Overview")  # With region highlights my_highlights <- list(   "ATAC_peaks" = list(     regions = atac_peaks,  # data.frame with chr, start, end     tracks = "ATACseq",     color = "#FF000033"    # red with transparency   ),   "shared_peaks" = list(     regions = shared_peaks,     tracks = "all",        # highlight on all signal tracks     color = "#0000FF33"    # blue with transparency   ) ) AETHER_create_circos(circos_data, output = "circos.png",                       highlights = my_highlights)  # With annotation chords (Phase 2B) # annotation_regions should have chr, start, end, annotation columns # (compatible with APOLLO_annotate_peaks() output) annotated_peaks <- APOLLO_annotate_peaks(my_peaks, txdb)  # Optional: simplify annotation labels annotated_peaks$annotation <- gsub("Distal Intergenic", "Intergenic",                                     annotated_peaks$annotation)  AETHER_create_circos(circos_data, output = "circos_with_chords.png",                       annotation_regions = annotated_peaks,                       show_chords = TRUE,                       chord_alpha = 0.4)  # Custom annotation colors my_anno_colors <- c(   "Promoter" = "#E78AC3",   "Intron" = "#66C2A5",   "Exon" = "#8DA0CB",   "Intergenic" = "#FC8D62" ) AETHER_create_circos(circos_data, output = "circos_custom.png",                       annotation_regions = annotated_peaks,                       annotation_colors = my_anno_colors) } # }

title: Plot Genome Coverage Tracks — AETHER_plot_coverage_tracks
text: Produces genome browser-style stacked coverage track plot specified genomic region. named track shows read pileup signal filled area curve. Multiple files per track averaged single signal; optional variance ribbon can displayed replicates provided. Two input modes supported — provide exactly one: BigWig mode (bigwig_files): reads signal pre-computed BigWig files. Use BigWigs already exist (e.g. ELEUTHIA_bed_to_bigwig()). BED mode (bed_files): computes coverage --fly requested region directly fragment-level BED files via ELEUTHIA_bed_region_coverage(). efficient small region needed BigWig files pre-generated. optional peak annotation track can added bottom. Additional annotation tracks (e.g. CpG islands, methylation sites) can added via annotation_tracks.

title: Plot Genome Coverage Tracks — AETHER_plot_coverage_tracks
text: bigwig_files Track input. Two formats accepted: Flat (current default): named list named character vector element character vector BigWig file paths one track. tracks share common y-axis scale_y = "fixed". Grouped: named list named lists/character vectors. outer element defines group tracks (e.g. one omics type). scale_y = "fixed", y-axis fixed within group allowed differ across groups, tracks different dynamic range (e.g. ATAC vs RNA) forced onto scale. Example:   Mutually exclusive bed_files. bed_files Named list character vectors, one element per track. element character vector fragment-level BED file paths. Coverage computed --fly requested region . named character vector accepted shorthand. Mutually exclusive bigwig_files. Requires chrom_sizes. region Genomic region display. One : Character string: "chr1:1000000-2000000" Named character vector: c(chr="chr1", start="1000000", end="2000000") GRanges object (single range) chrom_sizes Required using bed_files. Exact chromosome lengths named numeric vector APOLLO_get_chromosome_sizes() data.frame. Ignored BigWig mode. normalize Character. Normalization BED mode : "CPM" (default) "raw". Ignored BigWig mode (signal already normalized file). bin_size Integer. Bin width bp BED mode . Default 10. Ignored BigWig mode. peak_bed Optional. Peak annotation track displayed coverage tracks. Either path BED file data.frame least three columns (chr, start, end). Equivalent adding "region" type entry annotation_tracks named "Peaks". annotation_tracks Optional named list additional annotation tracks display coverage tracks (peak_bed provided). element named list describing one track. Two types supported: type = "region" Genomic intervals shown filled rectangles (e.g. CpG islands, repeats). Required field: data (BED file path data.frame chr/start/end columns). Optional fields: color (fill colour, default "steelblue4"), height (relative patchwork height, default = annotation_height). type = "score" Per-site scores shown lollipop plot — vertical segment 0 score, capped point, coloured score value (e.g. methylation fractions). Required field: data (BigWig file path). Optional fields: color_low (colour score=0, default "steelblue"), color_high (colour score=1, default "firebrick"), score_limits (numeric(2), y-axis colour scale limits; auto-detected data NULL), height (relative patchwork height, default = annotation_height * 2). type = "genes" Collapsed IGV-style gene model track. Shows intron backbone, exon blocks (UTR height), CDS blocks (taller), strand direction arrows, italic gene name labels. Multiple genes automatically stacked rows avoid overlap. Required field: either txdb (TxDb object APOLLO_make_txdb() — fast, preferred) gtf_file (path GTF — slower, reads genome-wide). GO ontology: "BP" (default), "MF", "CC".  one ontology per call. top_n Integer. Top N enriched GO terms per module (p-value) include building DAG.  Default: 20L. min_ancestor_freq Integer. Minimum number enriched terms ancestor node must ancestor order retained.  Enriched terms always kept.  Lowering value shows context; raising focuses shared hubs .  Default: 2L. max_depth Integer NULL.  Maximum number levels traverse upward enriched terms.  NULL traverses way ontology root.  Default: 4L. show_shared Logical.  FALSE (default), enriched term coloured single best-p module.  TRUE, terms found multiple modules get combined label (e.g., "C1-C2") distinct auto-assigned colour. edge_types Character vector.  GO relationship types include edges.  combination "is_a", "part_of", "regulates", "positively_regulates", "negatively_regulates".  Default: five. node_size_range Numeric vector length 2.  Min max point sizes enriched nodes (scaled -log10(p)).  Default: c(3, 10). palette Named character vector.  Module name → hex color mapping. title: GO DAG Plot coloured by module — AETHER_plot_go_dag
text: Algorithm: Filters enrichment_result$combined requested ontology takes top top_n terms per module p-value. Traverses GO DAG upward (child → parent) enriched terms using GO.db::GOBPPARENTS (MF/CC), max_depth levels. ancestor node, counts many enriched terms ancestor .  Ancestors min_ancestor_freq removed. Renders filtered DAG ggraph using Sugiyama (layered/hierarchical) layout.  Enriched nodes coloured module group; ancestor nodes grey.  Edge line type encodes GO relationship. Required packages: GO.db (Bioconductor), ggraph, igraph (already Suggests).

code: AETHER_plot_go_treemap(   enrichment_result,   orgdb,   ont = "BP",   top_n = 20L,   threshold = 0.7,   method = "Rel",   show_shared = FALSE,   show_group_labels = TRUE,   min_label_scale = 0.1,   palette = NULL,   title = NULL,   verbose = TRUE )

title: GO Term Treemap via Semantic Similarity Reduction — AETHER_plot_go_treemap
text: enrichment_result gost_enrichment object APOLLO_enrich_gost DEMETER_load_enrichment, plain data.frame least columns term_id, source, p_value, module. orgdb OrgDb object (e.g. org.Hs.eg.db) package name string (e.g. "org.Hs.eg.db") passed rrvgo::calculateSimMatrix() rrvgo::reduceSimMatrix(). Required — load package first library(org.Hs.eg.db) (human) library(org.Mm.eg.db) (mouse), pass object. ont Character vector. GO ontology/ontologies plot. One "BP", "MF", "CC". Multiple values produce one panel per ontology single figure. Default: "BP". top_n Integer. Top N GO terms per module (p-value) pooled semantic reduction.  Higher values include terms may slow rrvgo::calculateSimMatrix().  Default: 20L. threshold Numeric (0–1). Similarity threshold rrvgo::reduceSimMatrix().  Higher values → fewer, broader clusters; lower values → , finer clusters.  Default: 0.7. method Character. Semantic similarity measure passed rrvgo::calculateSimMatrix().  One "Rel" (default), "Wang", "Lin", "Resnik", "Jiang". show_shared Logical. FALSE (default), GO term assigned single module best (lowest) p-value term ("winner takes ").  TRUE, terms found multiple modules assigned combined group labelled "C1-C2" (module names joined "-", sorted alphabetically) given distinct color automatically; useful spotting convergent biology across modules. show_group_labels Logical. TRUE (default), large parent-cluster tile shows module group attribution beneath semantic cluster name, e.g. "immune response\n(C7)".  group shown one assigned cluster's representative (highest-scoring) term. Set FALSE display semantic cluster name . min_label_scale Numeric (0–1). Minimum text scaling fraction passed treemap's lowerbound.cex.labels.  tile small fit text full fontsize.labels, treemap scales text ; required scale falls value label suppressed entirely.  Default 0.1 permissive treemap's default 0.4, labels appear small tiles.  Set 0 force labels regardless tile size (may produce small text).  Opening larger graphics device calling function also helps, larger tiles require less scaling. palette Named character vector. Module name → hex color mapping. NULL (default), colors auto-assigned internal 20-color categorical palette.  Unknown modules fall back auto-generated colors.  combined/shared group always uses "#AAAAAA" regardless palette. title Character. Main plot title.  NULL (default), ontology label used (e.g., "GO Biological Process").  multiple ontologies requested, ontology label appended automatically. verbose Logical. Print progress messages.  Default: TRUE.

title: GO Term Treemap via Semantic Similarity Reduction — AETHER_plot_go_treemap
text: Invisibly returns named list reducedTerms data.frames (one per ontology, named ontology code: "BP", "MF", "CC").  primary output treemap rendered current graphics device. Save png() / pdf() wrappers calling.

title: GO Term Treemap via Semantic Similarity Reduction — AETHER_plot_go_treemap
text: Workflow: Filters combined enrichment table requested GO source(s). Takes top top_n terms per module p-value pools . unique GO term, uses best (lowest) p-value across modules rrvgo score (-log10(p)). Computes semantic similarity matrix via rrvgo::calculateSimMatrix() (requires relevant OrgDb package). Reduces representative clusters via rrvgo::reduceSimMatrix(). Assigns term module group (winner shared, per show_shared). Renders via treemap::treemap() parent clusters outer groupings individual terms inner tiles coloured module group. OrgDb auto-detection: organism read enrichment_result$metadata$organism (set automatically APOLLO_enrich_gost()).  Supported organisms OrgDb packages: hsapiens → org.Hs.eg.db; mmusculus → org.Mm.eg.db; rnorvegicus → org.Rn.eg.db; drerio → org.Dr.eg.db; dmelanogaster → org.Dm.eg.db; celegans → org.Ce.eg.db; scerevisiae → org.Sc.sgd.db; sscrofa → org.Ss.eg.db; btaurus → org.Bt.eg.db; cfamiliaris → org.Cf.eg.db; ggallus → org.Gg.eg.db. corresponding OrgDb package must installed. Required packages: rrvgo (Bioconductor) treemap (CRAN), plus appropriate OrgDb package organism.

title: GO Term Treemap via Semantic Similarity Reduction — AETHER_plot_go_treemap
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(org.Hs.eg.db)  # human; use org.Mm.eg.db for mouse  # Basic GO:BP treemap AETHER_plot_go_treemap(gost_res, orgdb = org.Hs.eg.db)  # Multiple ontologies side by side AETHER_plot_go_treemap(gost_res, orgdb = org.Hs.eg.db, ont = c("BP", "MF"))  # Show shared terms across modules in grey AETHER_plot_go_treemap(gost_res, orgdb = org.Hs.eg.db, show_shared = TRUE)  # Custom module palette + save to PNG my_pal <- c(C1 = "#E41A1C", C2 = "#377EB8", C3 = "#4DAF4A") png("treemap_BP.png", width = 10, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300) AETHER_plot_go_treemap(gost_res, orgdb = org.Hs.eg.db, ont = "BP", palette = my_pal) dev.off() } # }

title: Static PPI Network Plot — AETHER_plot_ppi_network
text: graph igraph object (e.g., APOLLO_get_ppi()). color_by Node coloring. One : Named vector: gene -> value (numeric gradient, character/factor discrete). E.g., cluster assignments log2FC values. "degree": Color node degree (connectivity). "betweenness": Color betweenness centrality. Single color string: uniform color (e.g., "steelblue"). NULL: default gray. size_by Node sizing. One : "degree" (default): Size connectivity. "betweenness": Size betweenness centrality. Named numeric vector: gene -> value. Single number: uniform size. layout Character. igraph layout algorithm. Default: "fr" (Fruchterman-Reingold). options: "kk" (Kamada-Kawai), "circle", "tree", "grid", "stress", "dh", "gem", "graphopt". show_labels Logical character. TRUE shows labels, FALSE hides , "hubs" shows labels top hub nodes. Default: "hubs". hub_n Integer. Number top hubs label show_labels="hubs". Default: 15. colors Color specification nodes. discrete: named vector colors. continuous: vector 2-3 colors gradient. Default: NULL (auto-selected based color_by type). edge_alpha Numeric. Edge transparency (0-1). Default: 0.3. edge_color Character. Edge color. Default: "gray70". size_range Numeric vector length 2. Min max node sizes. Default: c(2, 10). group_labels Named character vector. Maps discrete color_by group (e.g. PART cluster "C1", "C2", ...) label string (e.g. top enriched GO term APOLLO_enrich_gost()). One label placed centroid group's nodes. applies color_by produces discrete grouping (e.g. named character vector cluster assignments) — ignored warning continuous coloring ("degree", "betweenness", numeric named vector). Default: NULL (group labels). group_label_size Numeric. Font size group labels. Default: 3.5. group_label_color Character. Text color group labels. Default: "black". title Character. Plot title. Default: NULL (auto-generated). seed Integer. Random seed reproducible layouts. Default: 42.

what: Plot Signal Profile Heatmap (scale-regions layout) — AETHER_plot_profile_heatmap
title: Plot Signal Profile Heatmap (scale-regions layout) — AETHER_plot_profile_heatmap
text: Produces deepTools computeMatrix scale-regions-style figure. panel shows mean signal profile curve row-sorted heatmap. x-axis spans window bp upstream TSS scaled gene body window bp downstream TES. gene body scaled body_bins equal bins regardless gene length, genes different sizes directly comparable. Rows sorted descending total signal (highest top). Multiple samples displayed side--side one composite figure.

title: Plot Signal Profile Heatmap (scale-regions layout) — AETHER_plot_profile_heatmap
code: AETHER_plot_profile_heatmap(   bigwig_files,   txdb,   genes = NULL,   peaks = NULL,   window = 3000L,   bin_size = 50L,   body_bins = 100L,   colors = c("#A50026", "#D73027", "#F46D43", "#FDAE61", "#FEE090", "#FFFFBF", "#E0F3F8",     "#ABD9E9", "#74ADD1", "#4575B4", "#313695"),   profile_color = "#2166AC",   raster_interpolate = TRUE,   cap_quantile = 0.99,   cap_val = NULL,   profile_ylim = NULL,   max_genes = 5000L,   profile_height = 1,   heatmap_height = 5,   title = NULL,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Plot Signal Profile Heatmap (scale-regions layout) — AETHER_plot_profile_heatmap
text: bigwig_files Named list BigWig file paths. element character vector. multiple files supplied averaged one track. Element names become panel labels. Example: list(WT = c("wt1.bw","wt2.bw"), KO = "ko.bw") txdb TxDb object (APOLLO_make_txdb()). Used extract TSS TES positions (selected) genes. genes Optional character vector gene identifiers include. NULL (default) genes txdb used. Matched raw TxDb gene IDs NCBI "gene-" stripped forms. peaks Optional GRanges object path BED/narrowPeak file called peaks (e.g. ATAC ChIP). supplied, genes whose extended region (body ± window) overlaps least one peak retained. principled max_genes heuristic: rather guessing top-N genes TSS signal, provide exact loci interest. max_genes still acts hard cap result. window Integer. Base pairs upstream TSS downstream TES include flanking regions. Default 3000. bin_size Integer. Bin width bp flanking regions. number flank bins side = ceiling(window / bin_size). Default 50. body_bins Integer. Number bins gene body scaled , regardless gene length. Default 100. colors Character vector \(\ge\) 2 colours, ordered zero/low signal maximum signal, passed ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(). Default 11-stop red-yellow-blue diverging ramp (matching ColorBrewer/deepTools "RdYlBu" palette) gives low signal distinct red, mid-range signal pale yellow, high signal distinct dark blue — reproducing classic deepTools plotHeatmap look. Supply exactly 2 colours plain low/high linear gradient (previous behaviour). profile_color Character. Line fill colour profile curve. Default "#2166AC" (blue). raster_interpolate Logical. Passed ggplot2::geom_raster()'s interpolate argument. TRUE (default) bilinearly blends adjacent cells, avoids aliased/speckled look many gene rows downsampled shorter rendered image (typical max_genes thousands). Set FALSE crisp, unblended per-bin/per-gene pixels. cap_quantile Numeric (0,1). Signal values quantile capped display (shared cap across panels). Default 0.99. cap_val Optional numeric. Fixed colour-scale cap value shared across calls (e.g. mark-level global cap). NULL (default) cap computed per-call cap_quantile. profile_ylim Optional numeric. Fixed y-axis upper limit mean signal profile, shared across calls. NULL (default) limit computed per-call data. max_genes Integer NULL. Hard cap number genes displayed. peaks supplied limits peak-filtered set; peaks NULL TSS-signal pre-filter keeps top max_genes genes. Set NULL disable. Default 5000. profile_height Numeric. Relative height profile panel. Default 1. heatmap_height Numeric. Relative height heatmap panel. Default 5. title Optional character string. Overall figure title. verbose Logical. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

title: Run enrichment analysis using gprofiler2 — APOLLO_enrich_gost
text: gene_lists Named list gene vectors. Can ENSEMBL IDs (without version numbers), gene symbols, identifiers. organism gprofiler2 organism code. Common values: "hsapiens" (human), "mmusculus" (mouse), "rnorvegicus" (rat). Default: "hsapiens". sources Character vector data sources query. Options include: "GO:BP", "GO:MF", "GO:CC" (Gene Ontology), "KEGG" (KEGG pathways), "REAC" (Reactome), "WP" (WikiPathways), "TF" (TRANSFAC transcription factors), "MIRNA" (miRTarBase miRNA targets), "CORUM" (protein complexes), "HP" (Human Phenotype Ontology). Default: c("GO:BP", "KEGG", "REAC"). user_threshold Significance threshold term filtering. Default: 0.05. correction_method Multiple testing correction method: "g_SCS" (gprofiler's default), "fdr", "bonferroni". Default: "g_SCS". domain_scope Background statistical test: "annotated" (genes annotation), "known" (known genes), "custom" (provide custom_bg). Default: "annotated". custom_bg Custom background gene set (domain_scope = "custom"). min_term_size Minimum term/pathway size. Default: 1 (filtering, matches gprofiler online defaults). max_term_size Maximum term/pathway size. Default: 1e6 (effective upper limit, matches gprofiler online defaults). max_query_size Maximum number genes per query. Gene lists exceeding skipped. Prevents slow, uninformative enrichment large gene sets (e.g., WGCNA grey module). Default: 10000. Set NULL disable. significant Logical. include significant results combined/summary. terms always fetched gprofiler2 single API call regardless setting (filtering applied client-side), toggling incur extra requests. Default: TRUE. exclude_iea Logical. Exclude GO terms inferred electronic annotation. Default: FALSE. verbose Logical. Print progress. Default: TRUE.

text: peak_files Named character vector narrowPeak file paths. Names used set identifiers base output BED filenames. output_dir Directory save summit BED files. Created exist. half_window Integer. Half-width (bp) around summit. Total window = 2 * half_window. Default: 100 (200 bp total). chr_mapping Optional chromosome name conversion applied chr column writing BED file. Useful peak files use UCSC-style names (chr1, chr2) HOMER genome indexed NCBI accessions (e.g., NC_060925.1 T2T). Accepts: genome name string (e.g., "T2T") — uses built-mapping APOLLO_get_chr_mapping(), automatically reversed UCSC → NCBI direction. named character vector names source chr names values target chr names. NULL (default) — conversion. Peaks whose chromosome found mapping dropped warning. skip_missing Logical. TRUE, missing peak files skipped warning rather causing error. Default: TRUE. verbose Logical. Print per-set progress. Default: TRUE.

title: Get Chromosome Sizes from GTF/GFF Annotation File — APOLLO_get_chromosome_sizes
text: annotation_path Character string. Path GTF GFF file. Supports gzipped files (.gz extension). chromosomes Optional character vector chromosome names include. NULL (default), includes chromosomes found. Use filter standard chromosomes, e.g., c(paste0("chr", 1:22), "chrX", "chrY"). Note: filtering happens name_mapping applied. name_mapping Optional. Rename chromosomes NCBI accessions UCSC-style names. Can : character string built-mappings: "T2T" T2T-CHM13v2.0 named character vector: c("NC_060925.1" = "chr1", ...) add_chr_prefix Logical. TRUE chromosome names start "chr", adds prefix. Applied name_mapping (default = FALSE). cache_dir Character string. Directory store cached chromosome sizes. Default "data/" relative ZERO_DAWN root. Set NULL disable caching. cache_name Character string NULL. Name cached RDS file (without .rds extension). NULL, derives annotation filename. force Logical. TRUE, re-extract sizes even cache exists (default = FALSE). verbose Logical. Print progress messages (default = TRUE).

title: Get Chromosome Sizes from GTF/GFF Annotation File — APOLLO_get_chromosome_sizes

text: genes Character vector gene symbols include network. organism Integer. NCBI taxonomy ID. Default: 9606 (human). score_threshold Integer (0-1000). STRING's required_score (combined confidence score cutoff). Default: 400 (STRING's "medium confidence" default). network_type Character. "functional" (default; includes predicted/ indirect functional associations, STRING's website default) "physical" (direct physical binding interactions ). add_nodes Integer. Number extra first-shell interactors STRING add beyond query gene list. Default: 0 (within-list network , matching APOLLO_get_ppi()'s default behavior). image_format Character. STRING-rendered image download: "image" (default, PNG), "highres_image" (high-resolution PNG), "svg" (vector), "none" (skip image download entirely). image_path Character. File path save downloaded image. Required image_format != "none". verbose Logical. Print progress network summary. Default: TRUE.

title: Get protein-protein interaction network directly from STRING — APOLLO_get_string_ppi
text: list class "apollo_string_ppi" : graph igraph object — vertex/edge/graph attribute shape APOLLO_get_ppi()'s return value. string_ids data.frame. Raw STRING ID mapping query genes. interaction_df data.frame. Edge list STRING combined scores. image_path Character NULL. Path downloaded image, . params List call parameters used.

title: Get protein-protein interaction network directly from STRING — APOLLO_get_string_ppi
text: calls STRING REST API (string-db.org/api) directly HTTP using POST requests (via curl package), identifiers sent request body rather GET query string — avoids URL-length ceiling GET hits gene lists run hundreds (STRING's documented recommendation large identifier lists). Gene symbols first resolved STRING IDs via get_string_ids endpoint; genes fail resolve reported kept isolated nodes returned graph (parity APOLLO_get_ppi()'s n_query_genes/n_mapped_genes graph attributes). non-200 STRING API response, actual HTTP status code response body included error (rather generic connection-failure message GET-based url() connection give), make transient vs. persistent failures easier tell apart.

title: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (fgsea) — APOLLO_gsea
text: ranked_genes Named numeric vector. Names gene symbols (IDs matching gene sets); values ranking statistic (e.g. limma's t, DESeq2's stat, signed -log10(p)). Must names. gene_sets Named list character vectors (gene set name -> member genes), NULL fetch MSigDB via msigdbr. species Character. Species name passed msigdbr::msigdbr() gene_sets = NULL. Default: "Homo sapiens". db_species Character NULL. MSigDB species database query. NULL (default) lets msigdbr use default (human-centric, orthologs non-human species). Use "MM" query native mouse database (gene sets defined mouse studies native Mus musculus gene symbols, human orthologs). relevant gene_sets = NULL. collection Character vector. MSigDB collection codes fetch gene_sets = NULL. Default: c("H", "C2", "C5"). subcollection can appended colon (e.g. "C2:CP:REACTOME", "C5:GO:BP"). Mouse-native collections (db_species = "MM") use M-prefixed codes (e.g. "MH", "M2", "M5"). min_size Integer. Minimum gene set size (overlap ranked genes). Default: 15. max_size Integer. Maximum gene set size. Default: 500. fdr_threshold Numeric. FDR threshold $significant. Default: 0.05. verbose Logical. Print progress summary. Default: TRUE.

title: Link Differentially Expressed Genes to Nearby ATAC Peaks — APOLLO_link_degs_to_peaks
text: Identifies ATAC-seq peaks located within defined distance TSS differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Uses window-based approach captures peak-gene pairs within range (many--many), just single nearest gene per peak. Significance filtering applied deg_result caller passing function.

title: Link Differentially Expressed Genes to Nearby ATAC Peaks — APOLLO_link_degs_to_peaks
code: APOLLO_link_degs_to_peaks(   deg_result,   peaks,   gtf_file = NULL,   txdb = NULL,   distance = 50000,   gene_col = "gene_name",   chr_mapping = NULL,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Link Differentially Expressed Genes to Nearby ATAC Peaks — APOLLO_link_degs_to_peaks
text: deg_result DEA result. Either artemis_dea S3 object ARTEMIS_perform_dea(), plain data.frame. data.frame must contain minimum gene name column (see gene_col). peaks Peak data. Either data.frame least three columns (chr, start, end — BED-style 0-based starts) GRanges object. gtf_file Character. Path GTF/GFF annotation file. Used extract TSS positions. Either gtf_file txdb must provided. given, gtf_file takes precedence. txdb TxDb object (APOLLO_make_txdb()). Alternative gtf_file. Gene IDs TxDb must match values gene_col deg_result (e.g. use gene symbols). distance Numeric. Maximum distance bp peak (edge) TSS pair included. Default 50000 (50 kb). gene_col Character. Column deg_result holding gene symbols. Default "gene_name". chr_mapping Character named vector. Chromosome renaming apply gene coordinates GTF match peak coordinates. Pass "T2T" T2T-CHM13 NCBI→UCSC mapping. Ignored using txdb (mapping applied TxDb creation time). Default NULL (renaming). verbose Logical. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

title: Link Differentially Expressed Genes to Nearby ATAC Peaks — APOLLO_link_degs_to_peaks
text: S3 object class "apollo_deg_peaks" (named list): $linked data.frame. One row per peak × DEG pair within distance. Contains columns deg_result, plus peak coordinates, TSS position, distance_to_tss (signed: negative = peak upstream TSS relative transcription direction, positive = downstream). $deg_summary data.frame. One row per input DEG. Includes deg_result columns plus has_peak (logical), n_peaks (integer), nearest_peak_distance (bp). $peak_summary data.frame. One row per input peak. Includes peak coordinates plus near_deg (logical), n_degs, nearest_deg (gene name), nearest_deg_distance. $stats Named list summary counts. $params Named list parameters used.

title: Link Differentially Expressed Genes to Nearby ATAC Peaks — APOLLO_link_degs_to_peaks
text: Signed distance convention (strand-aware): + strand: distance_to_tss = peak_midpoint - TSS_position - strand: distance_to_tss = TSS_position - peak_midpoint Negative values = peak upstream (regulatory region); positive = downstream (gene body beyond). TSS extraction: using gtf_file, gene-level records read, making import fast even large annotation files. 5' TSS per gene symbol used (transcription direction). Gene name read gene_name gene GTF attribute (tried order).

text: regions data.frame columns: chr, start, end. Additional columns preserved. Coordinates 0-based (BED format). fasta_path Path FASTA file. Must accompanying .fai index (create samtools faidx). chr_mapping Either: NULL (default) - chromosome name translation genome name (e.g., "T2T") - uses built-mapping named character vector mapping region chr names FASTA chr names extend Integer. Extend regions many bp side extracting sequence (default = 0). Useful standardizing region sizes. min_width Integer. Minimum region width (extension) calculate composition (default = 100). Regions return NA values. include_repeats Logical. Calculate homopolymer dinucleotide repeat metrics (default = TRUE). include_sequence Logical. Include extracted sequence output (default = TRUE). text: regions data.frame: data.frame one row per input region. regions named list data.frames: named list data.frames, one per input set. data.frame contains: peak_id Region identifier (input generated) width Final region width extension gc_percent Percentage G+C bases at_percent Percentage +T bases n_Nbases Number N (ambiguous) bases longest_homopolymer Length longest single-base repeat (include_repeats) homopolymer_base Base forming longest homopolymer (include_repeats) longest_dinucleotide Length longest dinucleotide repeat bp (include_repeats) dinucleotide_motif Motif longest dinucleotide repeat (include_repeats) sequence actual nucleotide sequence extracted (include_sequence)

title: Calculate Sequence Composition for Genomic Regions — APOLLO_sequence_composition
text: Chromosome mapping: using genomes like T2T-CHM13 regions use UCSC-style names (chr1, chr2) FASTA uses NCBI accessions (NC_060925.1, NC_060926.1), use chr_mapping = "T2T" automatically translate. mapping applied internally - output retain original region chromosome names. Extension behavior: Consistent ELEUTHIA_expand_regions(), extend parameter adds specified bp side. extend = 50 adds 100bp total. Start coordinates clamped 0. Minimum width threshold: Regions smaller min_width (extension) return NA composition values. avoids unreliable percentages short sequences (e.g., 10bp regions base 10%). Repeat detection: Homopolymers: Consecutive identical bases (e.g., AAAA, TTTTTT) Dinucleotide repeats: Alternating two-base patterns (e.g., ATATAT, CGCGCG)

title: Compare multiple decoupleR methods — ARTEMIS_decoupler_compare_methods
text: list class "decoupler_comparison" containing: results Named list decoupler_result objects (one per method) summary Data.frame summarizing results across methods, built method's raw activity scores. Comparable "mean activity" across sources, comparable across methods methods differ output scale (e.g. wsum's unbounded weighted-sum scores vs. ulm/mlm's t-like statistics vs. viper's NES-like scores) – method much larger raw scale dominate mean_activity/min_activity/ max_activity regardless actual cross-method agreement. Use summary_zscored instead comparing/ranking across methods different native scales. summary_zscored columns summary, method's activity matrix z-scored (matrix-wide mean/sd, normalization consensus uses) per-source mean/sd/min/max/ agreement_score computed – puts methods comparable scale first, mean_activity ranking min-max range reflect actual cross-method agreement rather one method's raw output magnitude. Used AETHER_plot_method_agreement(scale =     "zscore"). correlations Method-method correlation matrix method_stats Per-method statistics consensus Consensus activity scores (consensus = TRUE) methods Methods used n_methods Number methods

title: Compare multiple decoupleR methods — ARTEMIS_decoupler_compare_methods

title: Differential Analysis for Count Data — ARTEMIS_differential_counts

Size factors batch correction settings inherited object. reference Character. reference/baseline group label (e.g., "WT"). denominator fold change calculations. experiment Character. experimental/comparison group label (e.g., "KO"). numerator fold change calculations. alpha Numeric. FDR threshold summary statistics (default = 0.05). verbose Logical. Print progress summary (default = TRUE).

title: Differential Analysis for Count Data — ARTEMIS_differential_counts
text: artemis_dea object (list) containing: results Data.frame per-feature DESeq2 results: feature_id, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj dds DESeqDataSet object analysis summary List summary statistics: n_features, n_sig_up, n_sig_down, n_tested, alpha comparison Character describing comparison (experiment vs reference) norm_counts Normalized count matrix (useful downstream analysis) Calling print() returned object reprints comparison significance summary (top 5 hits) without rerunning DESeq2 – see print.artemis_dea.

title: Differential Analysis for Count Data — ARTEMIS_differential_counts
text: Always call ARTEMIS_normalize_counts() full dataset first, pass result pairwise comparison. ensures: Size factors estimated samples, just two compared Batch correction configured one place applied consistently Normalized counts available visualization running DEA function subsets two groups interest, preserves pre-computed size factors, estimates dispersions, runs Wald test. Positive log2FC means higher experiment relative reference.

title: Differential Analysis for Count Data — ARTEMIS_differential_counts
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Step 1: Normalize full dataset (with optional batch correction) norm_data <- ARTEMIS_normalize_counts(counts, sample_sheet, batch_col = "batch")  # Step 2: Run each pairwise comparison dea_KO_vs_WT  <- ARTEMIS_differential_counts(norm_data, "WT", "KO") dea_OE_vs_WT  <- ARTEMIS_differential_counts(norm_data, "WT", "OE")  # View significant features sig_features <- subset(dea_KO_vs_WT$results, padj < 0.05) } # }

title: Fit Group LASSO for Variable Selection — ARTEMIS_fit_group_lasso
text: X Numeric matrix predictors (samples x features), typically POSEIDON_scale_predictors(). y Response vector. binary outcomes, 0/1 factor. continuous outcomes, numeric. groups Integer vector mapping column X variable group. Columns group number belong original variable. Typically encoded$var_mapping$groups. family Character string. Response type: "binomial": Binary outcome (logistic regression) "multinomial": Multi-class outcome (3+ categories) "gaussian": Continuous outcome (linear regression) "poisson": Count outcome (Poisson regression) penalty Character string. Penalty type: "grLasso" (default): Group LASSO - L1 penalty group norms "grMCP": Group MCP - non-convex, less biased estimates "grSCAD": Group SCAD - non-convex alternative nlambda Integer. Number lambda values regularization path (default = 100). lambda Optional numeric vector. Specific lambda values use. NULL (default), automatically generated. alpha Elastic net mixing parameter (default = 1 pure Group LASSO). Values < 1 add L2 penalty stability correlated predictors. group_names Optional character vector. Names group (nicer output). NULL, uses "Group1", "Group2", etc. verbose Logical. Print fitting summary (default = TRUE).

title: Fit Group LASSO for Variable Selection — ARTEMIS_fit_group_lasso

title: PART Clustering — ARTEMIS_part
text: Performs clustering using PART algorithm (Partitioning Algorithm based Recursive Thresholding). method recursively evaluates whether split clusters using Gap statistic dendrogram height threshold. detects multi-scale cluster structure guarding spurious splits.

title: PART Clustering — ARTEMIS_part
code: ARTEMIS_part(   mat,   q = 0.25,   min_size = 8,   B = 100,   Kmax = 10,   dist_method = "euclidean",   linkage = "average",   scale = FALSE,   seed = NULL,   verbose = TRUE )

title: PART Clustering — ARTEMIS_part
text: mat Numeric matrix features (genes) rows samples columns. Rownames used feature identifiers. Must contain NA – Gap statistic's reference generation (ref_gen = "PC") requires complete matrix svd(). Impute deliberately beforehand data real missingness (e.g. proteomics/mass-spec); PART NA-aware mode. q Numeric (0-1). Tuning parameter controlling splitting aggressiveness. Threshold = (1-q) quantile dendrogram heights. Lower q = less splitting. Default: 0.25. min_size Integer. Minimum features per cluster. Clusters smaller marked outliers (cluster C0). Default: 8. B Integer. Number bootstrap reference datasets Gap statistic. Higher = stable slower. Default: 100. Kmax Integer. Maximum clusters consider per recursive step. Default: 10. dist_method Character. Distance metric: "euclidean", "sq.euclidean" (squared Euclidean), "correlation" (1 - Pearson), "manhattan". Default: "euclidean". linkage Character. Hierarchical clustering linkage method: "average", "complete", "ward.D2", "single", etc. Default: "average". scale Logical. Z-score scale row (feature) clustering. Default: FALSE. seed Integer NULL. Random seed reproducibility. Default: NULL. verbose Logical. Print progress messages. Default: TRUE.

title: PART Clustering — ARTEMIS_part
text: S3 object class "artemis_part" containing: clusters Named character vector cluster assignments (C1, C2, ...; C0 outliers) cluster_map Data.frame gene, cluster, cluster_color columns n_clusters Number clusters (excluding outliers) n_outliers Number outlier features cluster_sizes Named integer vector cluster sizes cluster_colors Named character vector cluster hex colors dendrogram hclust object full dataset data (possibly scaled) input matrix, rows ordered cluster parameters List parameters used computation_time Elapsed time seconds

title: PART Clustering — ARTEMIS_part
text: PART algorithm works follows: Compute stopping threshold (1-q) quantile dendrogram heights Apply Gap statistic determine optimal k k > 1: accept split, recursively apply PART cluster k = 1 dendrogram height exceeds threshold: try splitting 2, recurse k = 1 height < threshold: stop (terminal cluster) Clusters smaller min_size marked outliers (C0) clustering, clusters reordered hierarchically similar clusters adjacent, labeled C1, C2, ... order.

title: PC-Metadata Association Test — ARTEMIS_pc_metadata_association
text: matrix Numeric matrix, features x samples (log2-scale). Must NA values — filter HADES_filter_olink_proteins() first needed. Rownames = feature IDs, colnames = sample IDs. sample_meta Data.frame one row per sample. Matched colnames(matrix) sample_col (rownames NULL). n_pcs Integer. Number top PCs test. Default: 10. ntop Integer NULL. Number variable features (row variance) use PCA. NULL = use features. Default: NULL. sample_col Character NULL. Column sample_meta holding sample IDs matching colnames(matrix). NULL = use rownames. Default: NULL. metadata_cols Character vector NULL. Columns sample_meta test. NULL = columns except sample_col. Default: NULL. scale Logical. Scale features unit variance PCA. Recommended NPX data proteins different dynamic ranges. Default: TRUE. categorical_threshold Integer. Variables many unique non-NA values treated categorical (Kruskal-Wallis). Variables unique values treated continuous (Spearman). Default: 10. verbose Logical. Print progress. Default: TRUE.

title: PC-Metadata Association Test — ARTEMIS_pc_metadata_association
text: S3 object class "artemis_pc_assoc" containing: pvalues Numeric matrix (n_pcs x n_vars). Raw p-values. effect_sizes Numeric matrix (n_pcs x n_vars). Spearman rho continuous variables; eta-squared categorical variables. test_used Named character vector. Test applied per variable: "spearman", "kruskal", "skipped" (degenerate variable). var_explained Numeric vector. Proportion variance explained per PC (e.g. 0.25 = 25%). pca prcomp object use custom plotting. params List parameters used.

title: PC-Metadata Association Test — ARTEMIS_pc_metadata_association
text: Test selection per variable: Continuous (> categorical_threshold unique values): Spearman rank correlation PC scores variable values. Categorical (<= categorical_threshold unique values, character/factor): Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test across groups. Skipped: variables one unique value, fewer 2 complete observations per group exist. Effect sizes: Spearman rho (range -1 1); eta-squared Kruskal-Wallis (H - k + 1) / (n - k), H test statistic, k number groups, n number observations. Negative eta-squared set 0.

text: sample_sheet data.frame. Must include columns identified sample_col bw_col. group_x Named list defining x-axis. See Details. group_y Named list defining y-axis. See Details. regions One : "bins" genome-wide fixed-width bins, path BED file (3-column, 0-based half-open), GRanges object. bin_size Integer. Bin width bp. used regions = "bins". Default 1000. genome Character NULL. Genome identifier (e.g. "hg38"). Used logging regions = "bins". Chromosome sizes derived BigWig seqinfo; parameter load BSgenome package. Default NULL. ratio Logical. TRUE, compute log2 ratio axis whose list exactly 2 names. Default FALSE. pseudocount Numeric. Added group means log2 ratio: log2((numerator + pseudocount) / (denominator + pseudocount)). Prevents log(0) dampens instability near-zero signal. Symmetric — introduce directional bias. Default 1. min_signal Numeric NULL. Regions representative signal axes falls threshold removed ratio computation. Representative = single group mean (1-name list) max(group1, group2) (2-name list). Regions enriched one group retained. Default NULL (filtering). sample_col Character. Column sample_sheet holding sample IDs. Default "sample_id". bw_col Character. Column sample_sheet holding BigWig file paths. Speeds multi-region workflows loading file . Default NULL.

title: Prepare BigWig Signal Data for 2D Density Scatter Comparison — ARTEMIS_prepare_bw_comparison
text: Input list logic: group_x group_y named list mapping group labels character vectors sample IDs: 1 name — direct mean signal across samples. E.g. list(CTRL = c("s1", "s2")). 2 names + ratio = TRUE — log2 ratio. first name denominator, second numerator: log2((2nd + pc) / (1st + pc)). E.g. list(CTRL = c("s1","s2"), TREAT = c("s3","s4")) yields log2((TREAT + pc) / (CTRL + pc)). Mixed axes valid (one direct, one ratio). Order operations: validate inputs → resolve paths → define regions → extract mean signal per BigWig → average replicates per group → filter (min_signal) → compute log2 ratio → return data frame.

title: Generate Multi-Dataset Simulations with Shared Latent Structure — DEMETER_generate_multi_datasets
text: n_datasets Integer. Number datasets generate (default = 3). n_samples Integer. Number samples dataset (default = 100). n_features Integer vector. Number features dataset. Must length equal n_datasets (default = c(500, 1000, 750)). signal_samples Integer. Number samples containing true signal shared latent variable (default = 25). Remaining samples noise. signal_features Integer vector. Number features containing true signal dataset. Must length equal n_datasets (default = c(50, 50, 40)). seed Integer. title: Generate Multi-Dataset Simulations with Shared Latent Structure — DEMETER_generate_multi_datasets
text: list following components: datasets List length n_datasets containing simulated data matrices. matrix dimensions n_samples x n_features. true_canonical List true canonical vectors (one per dataset). Signal features weight 1, noise features weight 0. shared_latent Matrix (n_samples x 1) containing shared latent variable. First signal_samples rows 1, remaining rows 0. signal_samples Integer indicating number signal samples. signal_features Integer vector indicating number signal features per dataset.

title: Generate Multi-Dataset Simulations with Shared Latent Structure — DEMETER_generate_multi_datasets
text: simulation model follows sparse CCA framework: dataset : $$X_i = u \cdot v_i^T + E_i$$ : u shared latent variable (n_samples x 1) v_i canonical vector dataset (n_features x 1) E_i Gaussian noise ~ N(0, 1) true signal sparse: first signal_samples samples non-zero latent values first signal_features[] features dataset participate shared structure simulation allows controlled testing : Feature selection accuracy (can methods recover signal features?) Sample selection accuracy (can methods identify signal samples?) Robustness noise Scalability varying dimensions

text: Reads DIA-NN report.pg_matrix file (.xlsx tab-delimited text), parses sample identifiers column names (Windows POSIX file paths DIA-NN output), log2-transforms intensities, returns structured massspec_data object. function performs QC filtering. remove controls, pool samples, high-missingness samples/proteins, pass result HADES_filter_massspec() HADES_filter_massspec_proteins().

title: Load DIA Mass Spectrometry Data (DIA-NN report.pg_matrix) — ELEUTHIA_load_massspec
code: ELEUTHIA_load_massspec(   ms_file,   sheet = 1,   metadata_file = NULL,   metadata_sheet = 1,   sample_col = "SampleID",   n_annotation_cols = NULL,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Load DIA Mass Spectrometry Data (DIA-NN report.pg_matrix) — ELEUTHIA_load_massspec
text: ms_file Character. Path DIA-NN report.pg_matrix file. Accepted formats: .xlsx, .tsv, .txt, .csv. sheet Integer character. Sheet read ms_file xlsx workbook. Default: 1. metadata_file Character NULL. Path sample metadata file (.csv, .tsv, .xlsx). Joined onto $sample_meta sample_col. Default: NULL. metadata_sheet Integer character. Sheet xlsx metadata files. Default: 1. sample_col Character. Column metadata_file used join key. Parsed sample IDs (numeric strings, SEP###-# labels, etc.) matched column. Default: "SampleID". n_annotation_cols Integer NULL. Number leading columns protein annotations rather sample intensities. NULL (default) uses auto-detection: annotation columns whose names contain file-path separator (/ \) .d extension. verbose Logical. Print loading progress. Default: TRUE.

title: Load DIA Mass Spectrometry Data (DIA-NN report.pg_matrix) — ELEUTHIA_load_massspec
text: S3 object class "massspec_data" containing: wide Numeric matrix: proteins (rows) x samples (cols). Rownames = Protein.Group. Colnames = parsed SampleID. Values log2-transformed intensities; zeros negatives become NA. sample_meta Per-sample data.frame: SampleID, SampleType, PlateID, plus columns joined metadata_file. protein_meta Per-protein data.frame annotation columns input file (e.g. Protein.Group, Protein.Names, Genes, First.Protein.Description). Rownames match rownames($wide). params List loader parameters used (provenance).

title: Load DIA Mass Spectrometry Data (DIA-NN report.pg_matrix) — ELEUTHIA_load_massspec
text: Expected input format: Column names must follow standardised convention produced project's prep_MS_data.R script: {SampleID}_Plate {N} (e.g. "1027_Plate 1", "SEP001-3_Plate 7", "pool1_Plate 12"). Raw DIA-NN file paths supported; data must prepared prep_MS_data.R first. Sample ID parsing: PlateID extracted _Plate N suffix; SampleID everything . Column names match _Plate N suffix pattern yield PlateID = NA SampleID = original column name. Sample type classification: identity guessed ID shape – column's SampleID can format. Instead: "POOL" — pooled QC injections (pool*). Present every plate batch drift monitoring. metadata entry expected. "SAMPLE" — non-pool column whose parsed SampleID found metadata_file (sample_col). biological distinction (group, timepoint, cohort) lives joined metadata columns, SampleType. "" — non-pool column match row metadata_file. Typically wells belonging different sub-study run plates/DIA-NN batch (e.g. sample-stability QC arm SubjectID/Group scheme tracked plate layout, main clinical metadata) rather malformed IDs. columns joined metadata dropped HADES_filter_massspec() default. metadata_file NULL, nothing check match , every non-pool column classified "SAMPLE". Log2 transformation: Raw DIA intensities linear scale. Intensities \(\le 0\) (zeros = detected; negatives = artefact) set NA log2() applied. transform passing ARTEMIS_limma_de(). Normalization: performed load time. Pass $wide POSEIDON_normalize_massspec() filtering.

title: Load DIA Mass Spectrometry Data (DIA-NN report.pg_matrix) — ELEUTHIA_load_massspec
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Load only ms_raw <- ELEUTHIA_load_massspec("report.pg_matrix.xlsx")  # Load with Olink-matched metadata, then filter ms_raw <- ELEUTHIA_load_massspec(   ms_file       = "report.pg_matrix.xlsx",   metadata_file = "olink_sample_meta.csv",   sample_col    = "SampleID" ) ms <- HADES_filter_massspec(ms_raw, keep_types = "SAMPLE") ms <- HADES_filter_massspec_proteins(ms, max_na_fraction = 0.5) ms$wide <- POSEIDON_normalize_massspec(ms$wide) } # }

title: Load Olink NPX Data — ELEUTHIA_load_olink
text: npx_file Character. Path Olink NPX file (.parquet .csv). metadata_file Character NULL. Path plate layout metadata (.xlsx, .csv, .tsv). Joined onto data sample_col. Default: NULL. metadata_sheet Integer character. Sheet read .xlsx files. Default: 1. sample_col Character. Column name present NPX data metadata used join key. Default: "SampleID". npx_col Character. NPX NAs propagated -. sample_meta Per-sample data.frame samples. Contains SampleID, SampleType, PlateID, WellID, SampleQC, plus joined metadata columns. assay_meta Per-protein data.frame: OlinkID, Assay, UniProt, Panel, warn_fraction (proportion samples AssayQC == "WARN"). params List loader parameters used (provenance).

text: bed_files Character vector paths BED files, named list loaded BED data.frames. merge_distance Integer. Maximum distance (bp) fragments merge single region (default = 150). min_fragments Integer. Minimum fragments retain candidate region (default = 10). noise filter - regions discarded merging. title: Select Regions Based on Fragment Count or Density Threshold — ELEUTHIA_select_regions
code: ELEUTHIA_select_regions(   candidate_regions,   min_fragments = NULL,   quantile_threshold = NULL,   max_width = NULL,   min_samples = NULL,   by_density = FALSE,   min_density = NULL,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Select Regions Based on Fragment Count or Density Threshold — ELEUTHIA_select_regions
text: candidate_regions Data.frame ELEUTHIA_merge_fragments() columns: chr, start, end, n_fragments, n_samples. min_fragments Integer NULL. Absolute minimum fragment count keep region. Ignored by_density = TRUE; use min_density instead. NULL, quantile_threshold used. quantile_threshold Numeric 0 1, NULL. Keep regions quantile. by_density = FALSE (default) quantile computed raw fragment count; by_density = TRUE computed fragment density (fragments per bp). E.g., 0.90 keeps top 10% regions. NULL, absolute threshold used. max_width Integer NULL. Maximum region width bp. Regions wider removed filter. Useful discarding broad, diffuse accumulations inflate raw fragment counts without genuine local enrichment. Default NULL (cap). min_samples Integer NULL. Minimum number samples must contributed least one fragment region retained. Requires n_samples column produced ELEUTHIA_merge_fragments(). filter applied max_width fragment count/density threshold, can substantially reduce candidate pool quantile computation. Default NULL (sample support requirement). by_density Logical. TRUE, threshold filtering performed fragment density (n_fragments / width bp) rather raw fragment count. normalises region width narrow, concentrated peaks preferred broad, diffuse ones equivalent total counts. Default FALSE (backward-compatible behaviour). min_density Numeric NULL. Absolute minimum fragment density (fragments per bp) keep region. used by_density = TRUE. NULL, quantile_threshold used. verbose Logical. Print selection summary (default = TRUE).

title: Select Regions Based on Fragment Count or Density Threshold — ELEUTHIA_select_regions
text: data.frame columns: chr, start, end, peak_id, n_fragments, n_samples, fragment_density, width. regions passing filters included. fragment_density always returned inspection.

title: Select Regions Based on Fragment Count or Density Threshold — ELEUTHIA_select_regions
text: Filters applied following order: max_width: remove regions wider cap min_samples: require fragment contribution least N samples Fragment count density threshold (whichever absolute quantile thresholds stringent) Applying min_samples quantile threshold intentional: quantile computed biologically supported subset, preventing low-support regions diluting distribution. Choosing count density mode: Raw fragment count (by_density = FALSE) reflects total signal accumulation appropriate region widths comparable. Fragment density (by_density = TRUE) normalises region width better matches RPKM-normalised BigWig tracks, making preferable merging step produces regions highly variable size.

title: Select Regions Based on Fragment Count or Density Threshold — ELEUTHIA_select_regions

title: Eleuthia - Sample Sheet Functions — ELEUTHIA_validate_sample_sheet
text: function operates two modes depending whether sample_id column present: Experimental mode (sample_id column): bio_rep, tech_rep, batch required, sample_id auto-generated <omics>_<group>_<bio_rep><tech_rep>_b<batch>. Cohort mode (sample_id column present): bio_rep, tech_rep, batch optional. provided sample_id values used directly validated uniqueness. Suitable public datasets (e.g., TCGA) sample unique individual rather replicate within experimental design. Required columns modes: file_loc: Directory containing data file file_name: Name data file group: Experimental group (e.g., "WT", "SMUG1_KO", "male", "female") omics: Type omics data (free-form label, e.g., "ATACseq", "CHIPseq", "RNAseq", "5hmu", "CUT&RUN", etc.) format: File format ("peaks", "bed", "counts") bed_loc: Path fragment BED file quantification (required peaks bed formats). Typically created bedtools bamtobed. Additional required columns experimental mode : bio_rep: Biological replicate identifier tech_rep: Technical replicate identifier batch: Batch number function performs following validations: Checks required columns present Removes empty rows Validates format values allowed types Checks data files exist (check_files = TRUE) Checks quantification BED files exist peak/bed formats (check_beds = TRUE) Generates unique sample_id row Note: omics column accepts string value. allows flexibility custom omics types (e.g., "5hmu", "CUT&RUN", "MeDIP") may processed similarly standard types. format column determines data loaded. experimental mode, sample IDs generated : <omics>_<group>_<bio_rep><tech_rep>_b<batch> timepoint column present, appended uniqueness: <omics>_<group>_<bio_rep><tech_rep>_b<batch>_t<timepoint>

what: Compute TSS Enrichment Score from BigWig files — HADES_tss_enrichment
title: Compute TSS Enrichment Score from BigWig files — HADES_tss_enrichment
text: Computes per-sample TSS enrichment scores BigWig files. TSS enrichment score standard ATAC-seq QC metric (ENCODE guidelines) quantifies specifically Tn5 inserted open chromatin near transcription start sites relative flanking background signal. score computed : Aggregating normalised BigWig signal across TSS windows single mean profile. Normalising mean signal outermost flank_bins bins side window (background estimate). Reporting maximum normalised profile enrichment score (typically centre bin TSS). ENCODE recommends score >= 6 human ATAC-seq data passing threshold. value derived empirically may universally appropriate — verify cell type coverage depth (Corces et al., 2018, Nature Methods, doi:10.1038/s41592-018-0105-7).

text: sample_sheet data.frame. Must contain minimum columns sample_id bw_loc (path BigWig file sample). optional condition column carried result used colouring AETHER_plot_tss_enrichment. Exactly one sample_sheet bw_file must provided. bw_file Character. Path single BigWig file. Use processing one sample without sample sheet. Exactly one sample_sheet bw_file must provided. txdb TxDb object. Used extract TSS positions. Create APOLLO_make_txdb() load pre-built TxDb annotation package. window Integer. Base pairs upstream downstream TSS include profile window. Default 3000L. bin_size Integer. Approximate width bin bp. window divided 2 * floor(window / bin_size) + 1 equal bins. Default 10L. flank_bins Integer. Number bins edge window used estimate background signal. Background mean outermost flank_bins side. default settings (bin_size = 10, flank_bins = 10) represents 100 bp background flank. Default 10L. threshold Numeric. Score threshold used flag samples passing QC. ENCODE recommended value 6 guideline human data; universally established threshold exists — treat reference point, absolute standard. Default 6. verbose Logical. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

text: X Named list matrices, one per view, samples rows features columns (GAIA's standard convention, HEPHAESTUS_multi_convCCA()). List names become MOFA2 view names. Views need samples sample order – rownames join key across views. groups Optional named character vector factor, sample ID -> group label, MOFA2's multi-group framework. Default NULL (single group). MOFA2's documentation describes multi-group advanced option recommended first approach – treat experimental. num_factors Integer. Number latent factors fit. Default 10 (MOFA2's package default). views samples, check variance_explained result rather assuming 10 appropriate – default tuned particular dataset. likelihoods Optional named character vector, view name -> "gaussian", "poisson", "bernoulli". Default NULL uses "gaussian" every view. MOFA2's guidance prefer transforming count/binary data continuous values rather relying non-gaussian likelihoods, give non-optimal results. spikeslab_weights Logical. Use spike--slab sparsity prior factor weights. Default TRUE (MOFA2 default). spikeslab_factors Logical. Use spike--slab sparsity prior factors. Default FALSE (MOFA2 default). scale_views Logical. Scale view unit variance training. Default FALSE. convergence_mode Character. "fast", "medium", "slow" – controls ELBO-change convergence threshold. Default "fast". maxiter Integer. Maximum training iterations. Default 1000. drop_factor_threshold Numeric. Fraction variance explained factor dropped training; -1 disables dropping. Default -1 (MOFA2 default). seed Integer. Random seed reproducibility. Default 42 (MOFA2 default). use_basilisk Logical. Let MOFA2 provision basilisk-managed Python environment mofapy2 backend. Default TRUE – unlike GAIA's basilisk-wrapped tools (CPAT, SignalP, Pfam, HOMER), .gaia_mofa_env exists GAIA/R/basilisk.R; MOFA2 manages . Set FALSE manually configured Python/mofapy2 installation via reticulate::use_python(). outfile Character NULL. Path save trained model (.hdf5). Default NULL uses temp file – pass explicit path intend reload model later HEPHAESTUS_load_mofa_model(), since temp files guaranteed persist across R sessions. verbose Logical. Print progress. Default TRUE.

Column $sample_meta containing batch information (default = "PlateID"). group_col Character string NULL. Optional column $sample_meta biological covariate preserve correction (default = NULL, covariate preserved). Samples NA column (e.g. POOL samples, biological group) assigned "no_group" level rather dropped, every sample still corrected. method Character string. "combat" (default) "limma". impute_method Character string. disposable working copy used make ComBat/limma runnable filled : "batchmean" (default) – missing cell filled protein's mean WITHIN batch (observed cells ). Falls back protein's global mean protein/batch combination zero observed values batch. "global" – missing cell filled protein's mean across samples, regardless batch (original behavior function). Comparing two SEPSOMICS dataset (see projects/SEPSOMICS/massSpec_imputation_comparison.R) showed "global" -corrects proteins high missingness given batch – placeholder pulls batch's estimate toward grand mean instead , diluting estimated batch effect. "batchmean" failure mode, established one dataset/filtering setup; "global" kept available case different experiment's missingness pattern behaves differently. verbose Logical. title: Normalize a Log2 Mass Spectrometry Intensity Matrix — POSEIDON_normalize_massspec
text: VSN (Huber et al. 2002, Bioinformatics): fits generalized log (glog/arsinh) calibration per sample via robust iterative regression raw intensity scale. Simultaneously normalizes cross-sample shifts stabilizes variance across full intensity range (heteroscedasticity correction) — proteins low high abundance treated equally. Output log2-like scale ("h" scale). pipeline stores log2 data ms$wide, VSN mode back-transforms (2^wide) fitting re-applies original NA mask , since vsn::justvsn() fitting driven observed values . Requires vsn Bioconductor package: BiocManager::install("vsn"). Median centering: subtracts per-sample median (non-NA values) column. Removes run--run location shifts log2 scale correct heteroscedasticity. Retained lightweight fallback comparison. analysis pipeline:
